rationale: The BOOK ENTRY's core equates the new name with a renewed Word/covenant/priesthood known-received-kept solely by its bearer. None of the printed references (Gen 32:28; Isa 62:2-5; 65:15; Rev 2:17) or the supplied chapter excerpts establish that equation; they show divine renaming that marks changed status, vindication, or intimate receipt. The common reading (God-conferred new identity/status) accounts for every textual detail—Jacob's prevailing, Zion's Hephzibah/Beulah, the servants' other name, the secret name on the white stone—with fewer unsupported steps and no need to import unstated referents (Word, covenant, priesthood). The chapter's brief link of Rev 2:17 to 'receives and keeps' is a secondary knowing-theme application that neither appears in the entry nor salvages its identification. The counter therefore explains the evidence better overall.
book_core_identification: The new name is itself a renewed Word, covenant, and priesthood that is known, received, and kept only by the one who bears it.
book_secondary_elaborations: known, received, and kept only by the one who bears the renewed Name
unsupported_glossary_assertions: identification of the new name as a renewed Word
identification of the new name as a renewed covenant
identification of the new name as a renewed priesthood
the claim that these are known/received/kept only by the bearer as the definition of the name itself
chapter_only_objections: The chapter's broader reduction of knowing/love/faith/belief to commandment-keeping is not asserted in the glossary entry and is set aside.
The chapter's parenthetical gloss that the Rev 2:17 name is 'known only by the one who receives and keeps it' is an application outside the printed entry.
strongest_counter_interpretation: In mainstream Christian reading the new name symbolizes the new identity, character, and status God confers on a redeemed person or people, marking decisive divine transformation, covenant belonging, and (in Revelation) final vindication and secure membership.
counter_core_identification: A God-conferred designation of transformed identity, character, and covenant status.
material_core_denial: The new name is not a renewed Word, covenant, or priesthood; it is the designation of the new identity/status given by God.
counter_case: Gen 32:28 explicitly renames Jacob 'Israel' because he has prevailed with God and men—identity and status change, not Word/covenant/priesthood.
Isa 62:2-5 supplies concrete new names (Hephzibah, Beulah) that reverse 'Forsaken/Desolate' and signal marital delight and national vindication visible to the nations.
Isa 65:15 contrasts the cursed name left to the wicked with 'another name' given to God's servants—again status reversal.

Rev 2:17 promises the overcomer a white stone bearing a new name known only to the recipient; the secrecy and personal receipt fit intimate belonging or private identity, not an equation with Word/covenant/priesthood.
The same pattern appears in the broader renaming corpus (Abram/Abraham, Sarai/Sarah, Simon/Peter) routinely cited for new identity/status.
counter_explanatory_advantages: Directly matches the explicit content of every cited renaming text without importing extra referents.
Unifies the OT prophetic and NT apocalyptic uses under one well-attested biblical motif (divine bestowal of new identity/status).
Accounts for both the public honorific names (Isa 62) and the secret personal name (Rev 2:17) as complementary facets of the same status change.
Requires no additional symbolic decoding steps beyond the plain sense of the verses.
evidence_book_core_cannot_explain: The concrete replacement names actually supplied in Isa 62:4 (Hephzibah, Beulah) and the reason given in Gen 32:28 ('for as a prince hast thou power…') have no natural link to 'Word, covenant, and priesthood.'
Isa 65:15's contrast between a name left 'for a curse' and 'another name' for the servants is status language, not a description of renewed cultic realities.
Rev 2:17's 'white stone' and 'no man knoweth saving he that receiveth it' are left unaccounted for by an equation with Word/covenant/priesthood.
